Plugins for [gajae-code](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/gajae-code) (`gjc`) that make an agent's work checkable.
A coding agent's own report ("tests pass", "the UI works", "I followed the plan") is a claim.

These plugins replace parts of that claim with evidence the agent cannot fake on its own: test runs recorded as private receipts with source freshness, browser assertions against a real page, plans validated against a fixed contract before they reach a tracker, and advisory second opinions labeled as advisory.
Every plugin states what it does not prove, keeps its results in a private store, and is installable on its own.

| [`verification-receipts`](verification-receipts/) | `verification_run` / `verification_status`: run explicit `node:test` files and keep an immutable receipt whose source freshness is recomputed on lookup. `verification_loop`: recheck that every delegated task was followed by covering verification. |

| [`jev-advisor`](jev-advisor/) | Advisory `fast` / `balanced` / `strong` tier advice before each delegated task, one-shot `jev_check` artifact checks and the read-only `plugin_metrics` report. Shadow by default; never routes models or proves quality. |
| [`rrsi`](rrsi/) | Exploration-trace store and deterministic Dream-RSI policy replay (`capture` / `import` / `dream` / `status`) with a due-gated `session_start` refresh. |
| [`rea`](rea/) | `rea_readiness` plus a workflow skill for the pinned [REA](https://github.com/morluto/rea) CLI (`rea-agents` 6.4.0). |
| [`wiki`](wiki/) | `wiki_query` over a guarded personal wiki and `wiki_propose` for pending proposals. Never approves or publishes. |
| [`aside-memory`](aside-memory/) | `aside_memory`: explicit, account-bound, read-only search over Aside memory, returned as quoted historical context. |
Measured attributes (tiers, counts, durations, journals) are descriptive observations, not quality, routing or causal proof.
Each bundle's generated `tools/` and `hooks/` are self-contained (sources are inlined at build time), so an installed plugin needs no sibling package.
GJC owns the installed code; plugins write only to their own directory under `~/.gjc-plugin/`.
Common: [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.4.x and Node.js ≥ 22 to build and test, and [gajae-code](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/gajae-code) (verified with 0.18.12) to install.

| `ui-regression` | 2 tools | The `aside` CLI with a connected profile and an explicit account; a page you serve on loopback | Runs drive a browser; `ui_regression_status` is offline. |

| `backplan` | 1 tool, loose skill | Nothing for the tool. Rendered issue bodies use Korean section headings; the optional skill registers issues through the maintainer's Linear MCP and trace helper. | Yes |
| `jev-advisor` | 3 tools, 3 hooks | `JEV_ADVISOR_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` for advice and checks | Without a key, advice is an explicit no-decision; `plugin_metrics` is offline. |
| `rrsi` | 1 tool, 1 hook | Nothing | Yes |
| `rea` | 1 tool, loose skill | Node.js `^22.19 \|\| ^24.11 \|\| >=26` or Bun; the first `npx` call downloads `rea-agents` | `rea_readiness` is offline; the CLI fetch uses the network. |
| `wiki` | 2 tools | A personal-wiki checkout with `scripts/wiki.py`, located by `WIKI_ROOT` (default `$HOME/jjongguet/personal-wiki`) | Local only |

Credentials live outside the replaceable installation tree, in `~/.gjc/agent/jev-advisor/.env` or the process environment (`JEV_ADVISOR_API_KEY` wins over `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`; process values win over the file).
Never put credentials in source or result records.
When upgrading several plugins, install `jev-advisor` first and `verification-receipts` second; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#install-order-and-replacement).
Without a local `gjc`, run the chain with `SELF_IMPROVE_SKIP_SMOKE=1 bun run test`; the four host smoke guards are then skipped and reported as skipped.
`bun run demo` drives three offline plugins through their committed tool surfaces, exactly as GJC loads them, under a temporary `HOME`.
It needs no key or network and checks that your real stores are untouched.
The `rea_readiness` lines depend on the Node/npx/Bun found on your machine.
Offline suites use disposable repositories and homes with synthetic or disabled transport; no live credential is required.
Host and browser smoke commands, and what each one does and does not prove, are in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#smoke-tests).

All plugin-owned result and state writes go to `~/.gjc-plugin/` (owned `0700` directories and single-link `0600` files; unsafe owners or modes, symlinks, hard links and corrupt inventories fail closed).
Inventory, record contents and retention bounds: [docs/private-results.md](docs/private-results.md).

[`self-improve/`](self-improve/) is a repository-native loop that proposes edits to this repository's own declared surfaces, checks them with deterministic guards in `git archive` scratch copies, and records every decision, including every rejection, in an append-only [ledger](self-improve/ledger.jsonl).
Measured campaigns and their limits are in [self-improve/evidence/](self-improve/evidence/README.md).
The [Harness² comparison](self-improve/HARNESS2.md) is a research proposal, not an installed capability.
Issues are welcome; pull requests from outside the maintainers are not accepted and are closed automatically.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup and the test matrix, [docs/agent-rules.md](docs/agent-rules.md) for the repository rules, and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) to report a vulnerability privately.

This repository ships plugins for [gajae-code](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/gajae-code) (`gjc`); each plugin directory is independently installable and its `gajae-plugin.json` is the version source of truth.
- **Bugs and feature requests:** open an [issue](https://github.com/jjongguet/gjc-plugin/issues/new/choose) using one of the forms.
- **Security problems:** report privately as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md); never in a public issue.

- **Pull requests:** not accepted from outside the maintainers. Pull-request creation is limited to collaborators, and a workflow closes any pull request whose author is not the owner, a member or a collaborator, with a pointer to issues. The workflow never checks out or runs pull-request code.
Maintainers land changes on `main` with conventional commit subjects in English.
Repository rules for agents and contributors are in [docs/agent-rules.md](docs/agent-rules.md).
- [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.4.x for builds and tests, Node.js ≥ 22 for the `node:test` runner, and a local `gjc` installation for runtime and smoke checks.
Without a local `gjc`, use `SELF_IMPROVE_SKIP_SMOKE=1 bun run test`; the four host smoke guards are then reported as skipped.

- `bun run build` builds every plugin (keyless). Generated surfaces under each plugin's `tools/` and `hooks/` are committed and must stay in sync; `bun run build:check` (or `bun <plugin>/scripts/build.mjs --check`) fails on drift without writing.

- `bun run test` runs the root chain: fixture tests for the repository check scripts (`scripts/tests/`), shared tests, per-plugin suites (`bun <plugin>/scripts/verify.ts`), the self-improve integration guards and the workspace checks.

- Suites are hermetic: disposable repositories/homes, synthetic or disabled transport, isolated fake CLIs. Live credentials, real personal data and production services are never required and never used in tests.

- Maintainers additionally run the workspace-standard validator, which lives outside this repository (`node ../shared/workspace-standard/validator/cli.mjs validate --root .`, profile `plugin-ts`). It is not required for external use.
Host smoke copies installed bundles into a private isolated GJC root and uses only a loopback provider; it does not mutate user configuration.

Jev result smoke imports installed hooks in a fresh isolated process and exercises bounded synthetic task/launch/terminal events — it proves hook/storage consumption, not a real child delegation or task quality.
Browser smoke requires an actually connected Aside profile and inspected owned loopback handlers.
Report source tests, installed dispatch, browser observations and real-provider judgment separately; never blend them into a single claim.
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every push to `main`: `build:check`, `evidence:check`, `docs:check`, `policy:check`, `bun run build`, the full test chain and `bun run demo`.
It has no `pull_request` trigger.

- Declare every installed surface (tools, hooks, skills) in `gajae-plugin.json`; keep generated surfaces keyless and reproducible from `lib/` + `src/` sources.

- Reuse the shared private-result primitives (`shared/`) when persistence is required. Transient wrappers such as `aside-memory` intentionally do not journal private payloads; never serialize arbitrary tool output as evidence.

## Install order and replacement

- `gjc plugin install <path> --user` refuses a plugin that is already installed. Replace one with `gjc plugin uninstall <name> --user` followed by `gjc plugin install <path> --user`; inspect the recorded source (`~/.gjc/agent/gjc-plugins/registry.json`) first.

- When upgrading several plugins, install **`jev-advisor` first** and **`verification-receipts` second**, then the rest, and run `gjc plugin doctor` afterwards. An older `jev-advisor` reading journal records written by a newer `verification-receipts` fails closed with `store_corrupt`.
- Rebuilding source alone does not update a running session. Tools and hooks load at **session start**; verify upgraded surfaces in a fresh `gjc` process.
- `dashboard/` — maintainer-only local meta view; not a plugin and not deployed. See [dashboard/README.md](dashboard/README.md).
- `steps.json` — the maintainer's manual release checklist (record, verify, human review); nothing runs it on a timer.
They are a contract, not background reading: the `rules-text` self-improve domain (`self-improve/domains/rules-text`) scores this file, and an edit must keep that domain green.
- Every plugin subtree names its installed, generated and verification surfaces, so an agent can work without guessing.
- An unverified change is never adopted.
- `jev-advisor/` — task-delegation tier advice, artifact checks and the read-only metrics report (advisory, never a gate).

- `self-improve/` — the repository's self-improvement loop. The append-only [ledger](../self-improve/ledger.jsonl) records every decision and [rrsi.json](../self-improve/rrsi.json) configures the loop.
- `wiki/`, `rea/`, `backplan/`, `aside-memory/` and `shared/` — the remaining plugins and the shared private-results module. Each plugin's `gajae-plugin.json` is its manifest of record.
- Full verification: `bun run test`; [package.json](../package.json) defines every script.
- Build: `bun run build`. Generated surfaces (`tools/`, `hooks/`) are build outputs; never edit them by hand.
- Never commit credentials, `.env` files or local key files; plugins read keys only from their documented locations outside the repository.
- Tests and demos run in disposable homes with synthetic or disabled transport; they must not write to a real `~/.gjc-plugin/` store or call a live provider.
- External pull requests are not accepted; report problems through issues.
## Records
- Committed evidence uses repository-relative paths; `bun run evidence:check` enforces this for `self-improve/`.
- The self-improve ledger is append-only. Never rewrite, reorder or delete a ledger row.
- Session logs, dated run notes and test counts do not belong in committed documentation; reproduction steps do.
## Commit and verification rules
- Stage only changed files; never `git add -A`.
- Use conventional commit messages, scoped to the plugin name where one applies.
